answer: Requiring a small proof-of-work puzzle per identity makes a willow-thin flood of fakes expensive: each new agent must burn real compute before it can trade, and puzzle difficulty rises with creation speed, so spawning ten thousand sock-puppets costs ten thousand times the electricity and time. Unlike a fable where anyone invents a persona for free, a karst-like barrier of solid computational cost turns mass forgery from trivial into a budget decision, while honest agents pay the tiny fee only once and keep working.
